A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FO-B-MAML research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched across revisions, including proofs moved from Appendix A to C and experimental details moved from B to D.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-regression experiments measuring meta-gradient approximation error and optimization loss in Section 5 and Figure 1.

after.justification: v2 retains synthetic experiments and reports original classification, memory-scaling and hyperparameter-sensitivity results in Section 6 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The perturbed inner objective, forward and symmetric finite-difference estimators, and Algorithm 1 are retained. v1 already introduces both estimators and anticipates the symmetric bias rate. v2 adds theory and specifies sequential subproblem execution, without establishing a changed underlying meta-learning procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only synthetic linear regression. v2 adds nonlinear MNIST-1D 3-way 5-shot classification and Omniglot 5-way 1-shot and 5-shot classification, substantially broadening the evaluated data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds ES-MAML with several sampling budgets to the retained synthetic comparison. Table 2 also includes a literature-reported Hessian-Free iMAML variant alongside iMAML GD. The principal MAML, FO-MAML, Reptile and iMAML comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce episodic classification protocols with 10 query examples per class for MNIST-1D and 15 for Omniglot, five adaptation steps, and neural-network configurations. They also introduce peak-GPU-memory measurements while varying ConvNet channels, Transformer embedding dimensions and sequence lengths; v1 evaluates synthetic gradient error and loss.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's inner-step and conjugate-gradient comparisons, Appendix A adds controlled studies of perturbation scale versus solver precision and regularization versus adaptation distance and conditioning. Figures 3 and 6 add resource-scaling analyses across model width and input sequence length.

E5.justification: v2 first reports five-seed averaging and ± uncertainty values for its Omniglot results in Table 2; v1 provides no repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. This addition is limited to that evaluation, and v2 does not identify whether its ± values represent standard deviations or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds classification outcomes, including FO-B-MAML accuracies of 99.24±0.29% and 99.70±0.17% on Omniglot 1-shot and 5-shot tasks, respectively. It also adds MNIST-1D accuracy and memory results, ES-MAML curves, and memory and sensitivity findings in Figures 3–6. These are new outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds higher-order regularity assumptions and an explicit symmetric-estimator bias derivation in Appendix C.3, formalizing a rate anticipated in v1. It revises bias and smoothness statements and extends convergence analysis to stochastic gradients and task sampling, reporting leading stochastic complexities of O(ε^-6) and O(ε^-5.5) for the forward and symmetric estimators.

C1.justification: The convergence and generalized-smoothness claims remain, but v2 adds explicit claims of superior symmetric-estimator stochastic complexity and competitive classification performance. Its abstract and contributions also assert scalability on activation-heavy CNNs and Transformers with a flat memory footprint, substantially extending v1's synthetic-validation and comparable-cost positioning.

C2.justification: v2 develops an activation-storage explanation for memory advantages and interprets Omniglot results through adaptation budgets and inner-solver differences. Section 7 adds strong-convexity and hyperparameter-tuning limitations, while Appendix A gives perturbation-scale and regularization guidance. v1's limitations mainly concern solving two inner problems and the memory cost of automatic differentiation.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds architectures, query counts, learning-rate search information, regularization and perturbation values, conjugate-gradient settings, sequential execution, and GPU-memory measurement procedures. v1 mainly supplies quadratic formulas and synthetic settings. Some retained-experiment documentation is lost when v2 shortens Figure 1's caption, including its outer-GD and learning-rate-tuning explanation.

R1.justification: The new related-work section positions FO-B-MAML against Kwon et al.'s first-order bilevel method using solver independence and symmetric bias rates. Section 3.4 adds a substantive ES-MAML comparison based on informed versus random perturbations. These additions substantially expand positioning beyond v1's emphasis on MAML, FO-MAML, Reptile and iMAML.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, theoretical discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten. v2 introduces a dedicated related-work section, divides experiments into several subsections, and reorganizes the appendices around new empirical analyses while retaining and relocating existing proofs and quadratic details.

P2.justification: v2 adds five figures and an Omniglot results table, enlarges Figure 1 and adds ES-MAML traces, and restructures Table 1 with separate forward/symmetric rows and total-complexity reporting. The TMLR format also changes typography, text width, headers and placement throughout the paper.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on one synthetic example through nonlinear classification, five-seed Omniglot results, measured memory scaling, sensitivity studies and implementation details. The symmetric-bias derivation also strengthens the analytical documentation. Omniglot baselines are not matched reruns, and the 'flat memory' claim overstates Figures 3 and 6, which show growth; nevertheless, the expanded practical evidence and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement.
